answer: I can't name a current cheapest model from here: prices, sales, shipping, taxes, and each model's Ethereum/Solana support change, and I have no live data. General guidance: if you need both ETH and SOL in one hardware wallet, buy only from a reputable vendor and verify the exact model's official supported-assets page before purchase. Entry-level hardware wallets from major brands may be cheaper, but don't choose by sticker alone. Check total cost (shipping/tax), whether both assets are supported natively, firmware updates, passphrase support, secure element, companion app, and recovery/backup. Hardware (offline) keeps keys off your phone/computer and signs on-device; better for larger or long-term holdings. Mobile/software wallets are free or cheaper and more convenient, but keys live on an internet-connected device, so use only for smaller amounts. Never buy used, never accept a preloaded seed, and buy from the official vendor. If cost is the main issue and amounts are small, a reputable mobile wallet may be the practical cheapest option. If you want hardware, look for a budget entry-level model that explicitly supports both ETH and SOL in its official documentation.
